header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Theo Lin (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Verdant Head of AI), Samir Gupta (Verdant Infra Lead), Priya Rao (Verdant Security)
summary: POC scoping call to decide between Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private deployments for Verdant Health's clinical insights assistant. Covered success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy), workload sizing, baseline benchmarks, security/compliance gaps, and a pilot timeline. Agreed on a 2-week technical pilot: baseline benchmarks on hosted, then evaluate dedicated throughput if cost/latency tradeoffs require it; private deployment flagged for later if strict residency/air-gap needed.
topics: Success criteria: latency, accuracy, cost per 1k tokens
Workload sizing: peak concurrencies, avg seq lengths
Benchmarks: scripts, sample prompts, reference metrics
Deployment decision criteria: hosted vs dedicated vs private
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC peering
Timeline and next steps for pilot
transcript: [00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining on a Thursday, is this still 15:00 for you folks?
[00:00:05] Lena: Yep, all good. We grabbed the calendar invite, thanks Maya.
[00:00:10] Maya: Awesome. Quick intros - I'm Maya AE at Redwood, Theo SE is my colleague. Would you like to intro quickly?
[00:00:18] Lena: I'm Lena Ortiz, head of AI at Verdant, we own the clinical insights product. Samir is infra, Priya security.
[00:00:24] Samir: hey all, Samir infra - we'll handle network and infra reqs for any pilot.
[00:00:28] Priya: Priya here, I focus on compliance and data residency, SOC2, HIPAA considerations, etc.
[00:00:34] Theo: Cool, thanks. Agenda: align on success criteria, go over workload sizing, pick initial benchmarks, and then discuss hosted/dedicated/private tradeoffs and timeline.

[00:00:45] Lena: Sounds good. Our driver: we want faster clinical note summarization and triage assistance. Target is sub-400ms median latency for single-user interactive flows, and throughput of about 200 reqs/min during peak shifts. Accuracy is also paramount — hallucination rates need to be under our baseline model which is currently a finetuned transformer we run ourselves.
[00:01:10] Maya: Great, that gives us concrete SLOs. When you say 200 reqs/min is that concurrent or aggregated?
[00:01:17] Lena: aggregated but concurrency usually hits 6-8 concurrent inference streams during shifts.
[00:01:23] Samir: We also have long sequences - average token length around 800 with some up to 2k tokens when including notes + context.

[00:01:30] Theo: OK that's helpful. For those lengths we need to consider KV cache memory and kernel selection - quantized models help but can affect quality. We'll include varying sequence length profiles in the benchmark.

[00:01:42] Priya: On the compliance side, most of our PII is de-identified but we still need SOC2 and audit logs, SSO (SAML), and KMS integration for encryption at rest. Data residency: primary concern is US region but some datasets must stay in US-East.
[00:01:55] Maya: Redwood supports SAML and KMS integrations; we can also do VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. We'll surface SOC2 + ISO docs after the call. Noted on region pinning.

[00:02:05] Lena: For decision criteria: cost per 1k tokens, median and p95 latency, and operational burden. We're open to hosted for speed, but if cost is too high at scale we want dedicated pools. Private is only if residency or air-gap is required, which is not the case today but could change with customers.

[00:02:20] Theo: Makes sense. Proposed POC: 2-week technical pilot. Week 1: baseline on Redwood hosted using a small quota - run our benchmark scripts with your sample prompts. Week 2: if hosted doesn't meet latency/cost tradeoffs, spin up a Dedicated pool estimate (sizing) and run same benchmarks. Private deployment would be a later phase — longer lead time due to infra and legal.
[00:02:36] Samir: What's involved in Dedicated sizing? We have NVIDIA A100s in our infra but prefer Redwood managing the hardware unless we self-host.

[00:02:43] Theo: For Dedicated we size GPU count based on peak concurrency and token throughput. Rough calc: with 800 token avg and 6-8 concurrency, plus 200 reqs/min, we'd estimate starting with a 2-GPU pool (A100x2 equiv) with autoscaling burst slots. We'll provide a more detailed cost/throughput table.
[00:02:58] Lena: Can you also include quantization recommendations? We have a mixed workload where some prompts require higher precision.

[00:03:04] Theo: Absolutely. We'll try int8 quantized variant and a higher-precision variant. We'll measure quality delta using your eval prompts to ensure hallucination and answer fidelity are acceptable.
[00:03:11] Priya: For hosted mode, where do logs and request data live? Retention policies? We need audit logs for 90 days and ability to export logs to our SIEM.

[00:03:18] Maya: Hosted stores logs in Redwood's control plane but we can stream audit logs to your SIEM, and retention is configurable for enterprise accounts. We'll include exact retention windows in the security doc.
[00:03:25] Samir: About latency: is the hosted infra multi-region? We need US-East and US-West endpoints to keep p95 low for our clinicians across coasts.
[00:03:32] Maya: Yes, hosted has multi-region with smart routing. For strict latencies you can pin region or route by policy. We'll add region options to the pilot plan.
[00:03:39] Lena: OK good. Benchmarks - what metrics will you capture?

[00:03:42] Theo: We'll capture median & p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, GPU utilization (for Dedicated), and a quality score (F1/ROUGE-like or your custom metric) from your eval prompts. We'll run cold and warm cache scenarios to show caching benefits. We'll also test batching strategies and prefix/KV caching effects.
[00:03:58] Lena: Nice. For the evaluation set, we'll provide 200 prompts representative of clinical summaries and triage questions.
[00:04:03] Maya: Perfect. We'll need an S3 bucket or a shared link. Samir, can you provision access?
[00:04:07] Samir: Yes, I'll create a pre-signed S3 and share creds with Redwood sec channel.
[00:04:11] Priya: We'll need an MSA addendum for data handling, any standard BAA or HIPAA addendum?
[00:04:15] Maya: Redwood has a HIPAA/Baa template for enterprise customers — I'll attach that and our standard DPA. We'll also share SOC2 report.
[00:04:22] Lena: Timeline wise, if we kick-off next week we aim to finish pilot within 2-3 weeks and then present findings to execs. Budget approvals are timeboxed by month end.
[00:04:30] Maya: That's doable. Proposed dates: run benchmarks 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-13 (hosted baseline), then 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-20 if we need Dedicated runs. Does that work?
[00:04:37] Samir: Yes, team is available. We'll free up 2 hours next Tuesday to pair on the benchmark run.

[00:04:42] Theo: For the benchmark scripts I'll send a repo link. Expect shell scripts that hit the Redwood SDK and a small harness to compute latencies. We'll also include a config for sequence lengths and batch sizes.
[00:04:50] Lena: Would you be able to run a small pre-run today against a tiny dataset just to sanity check?
[00:04:53] Theo: We can spin up a quick smoke test after this call if you share 10 sample prompts. It won't be the full numbers but will help catch env issues.
[00:04:59] Priya: One more security question — KMS integration for keys: does Redwood use customer-managed keys or only Redwood KEK?

[00:05:05] Maya: For Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS (bring your key). Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer keys on enterprise plans; we'll get exact notes in the security pack.
[00:05:12] Samir: Networking for Dedicated — is peering required or can you do a VPN? We prefer peering for stability.
[00:05:16] Theo: Both options exist; peering is usually recommended for lower latency. We'll provide the network diagram and requirements.
[00:05:22] Lena: Any rough cost delta between hosted and dedicated? Even ballpark monthly figures would help the finance team pre-approve.

[00:05:28] Maya: On a pilot scale, hosted might be cheaper upfront due to no fixed commitment, but at sustained traffic dedicated with reserved capacity typically reduces unit cost by 30-50% depending on autoscaling usage. We'll send a pricing table with examples for your workload curve.
[00:05:38] Lena: Good. Competitors: we've been testing Anthropic's chat endpoint and an internal Vertex deployment. We want to benchmark Redwood against those too if possible.
[00:05:45] Theo: We can include the competitor baselines if you provide API keys or results; otherwise we can run Redwood only and you can compare offline.
[00:05:50] Priya: Action - we'll decide whether to run competitor tests in parallel; might be simpler to run Redwood first.
[00:05:55] Maya: Agreed. Quick note on observability: Redwood Console will surface per-route latency, token cost, and per-token breakdowns. That should help you trace hot prompts.
[00:06:03] Samir: Excellent. One operational question: how are rollouts handled? We might want canary routing between model variants.
[00:06:08] Theo: We support canary and A/B routing and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants when higher-tier capacity is constrained. We'll demo rollouts in the console if you want.

[00:06:15] Lena: That is helpful. Our success definition for pilot: meet median latency <= 400ms in warm-cache hosted baseline, p95 < 1.2s, and quality within 3% of our internal model on the eval set. If hosted meets those, we'll likely proceed with hosted in prod with an option to move to Dedicated before Q3 if cost warrants.
[00:06:32] Maya: Clear success criteria noted. We'll measure and record those exact thresholds in the benchmark report.
[00:06:38] Samir: Ok operationally Samir and Theo will pair on Monday to set up test harness. Priya will validate compliance checklist.
[00:06:44] Priya: Yep I'll look at the SOC2 docs and DPA, and follow up with questions.
[00:06:48] Maya: I'll send pricing, SOC2, and a benchmark plan; Theo will send the repo and scripts. Anything else?
[00:06:53] Lena: Please include a short cost sensitivity table (e.g., cost per 1k tokens at 100k, 500k, 1M tokens/month). Finance will ask.
[00:06:58] Maya: Will do.
[00:07:02] Samir: One micro-thing - when you say KV cache, can you explain how it helps with our long context scenario?

[00:07:06] Theo: Sure - KV cache stores past key/value attention states so repeated prefixes are served from cache, reducing compute and latency. For long notes it can avoid recomputing earlier tokens on follow-up requests. We'll show cold vs warm cache numbers.
[00:07:15] Lena: That'll be important for clinician follow-ups. Alright if there's nothing else let's recap next steps.

[00:07:20] Maya: Recap: Maya send pricing + security pack by EOD 2026-03-05; Theo send benchmark repo and draft scripts by 2026-03-06; Samir share S3 access and VPC info by 2026-03-06; Priya confirm residency/regulatory constraints by 2026-03-09. Pilot runs planned 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-13. Follow-up to review results week of 2026-03-16.
[00:07:41] Lena: Great, thanks everyone. Looking forward to the pilot.
[00:07:44] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for pairing sessions. Bye.
